claims.text: HfZrTiTa0.53 has quasi-static yield strength of 786 MPa, compressive strength of 1314 MPa, and fracture strain of 13.5%.
The intervention adds Nb and V, adjusts Ta content, and uses repeated suspension melting.
Adding Nb and V while optimizing Ta will stabilize a dual-phase BCC microstructure.
The modified microstructure will contain a stabilized primary BCC phase and fine secondary-phase precipitates.
Nb and V additions will lower the alloy's stacking-fault energy.
Nb and V additions will promote fine-scale secondary phases in the BCC matrix.
The proposed microstructure will improve dynamic strain partitioning.
Fine secondary phases will hinder rapid strain localization.
Improved strain partitioning and delayed localization will enhance dynamic strain hardening and prolong uniform plastic deformation.
The modified alloy will exhibit approximately 10–20% higher yield and compressive strength than the baseline.
The modified alloy may exhibit a 15–25% improvement in fracture strain before localization.
The modified alloy will have greater uniform-deformation capability than the baseline.
The intervention will reduce impact-induced energy release through more effective energy absorption.
The predicted improvements apply under adiabatic dynamic loading at strain rates around 10^3 s^-1.
The effects may be weaker or absent at lower strain rates or under isothermal conditions.

contradictions.description: The baseline is defined as the unmodified alloy's quasi-static performance, while the prediction concerns dynamic loading and the falsification experiment compares both materials dynamically. Thus, the stated comparison baseline is inconsistent with the matched dynamic control actually required by the experiment.
